relax-arrive-01.text: You can pause here. Find a comfortable place, and let the next thing wait for a moment.

relax-arrive-02.text: There is nothing to finish in this little corner. Just settle in at your own pace.

relax-arrive-04.text: Take the space you need. You can listen, look around, or simply sit quietly.

relax-arrive-03.text: For a moment, you do not have to choose what comes next. Let yourself arrive.

relax-arrive-05.text: You have found a little pause in the day. There is no right way to spend it.

relax-arrive-06.text: Let this be a small landing place. The rest of the day can wait outside for a moment.

relax-arrive-07.text: You do not need a good reason to rest. A comfortable seat is enough to begin.

relax-arrive-10.text: We can leave a little silence around this moment. You do not have to fill it.

relax-arrive-08.text: Stay for one thought, or stay a little longer. You decide what feels useful.

relax-arrive-09.text: Here is a little room to slow down. No score, no catching up, no instructions to complete.

relax-scroll-03.text: You can leave the feed unfinished. There is no last post you need to reach.

relax-scroll-01.text: The next post can wait. If you like, set your phone down after this and look around your room.

relax-scroll-02.text: You noticed that you want a break from scrolling. That is enough for a new choice right now.

relax-scroll-04.text: Try giving your eyes one ordinary thing to rest on, away from the screen.

relax-scroll-05.text: A pause does not have to become a productive activity. You can simply stop for a while.

relax-scroll-06.text: If it helps, move the phone a little further away. Make this next moment easier to choose.

relax-scroll-08.text: Let the stream of other people’s updates carry on without you for a moment.

relax-scroll-07.text: You do not have to make up for the time you spent scrolling. Start with where you are.

relax-scroll-09.text: Pick something small beyond the screen: a window, a cushion, the light on a wall.

relax-scroll-10.text: When this clip ends, you can close your eyes if comfortable, or leave the screen and keep them open.

relax-overwhelmed-01.text: You do not have to untangle everything at once. Choose one small thing that would make this moment easier.

relax-overwhelmed-02.text: If decisions feel heavy, make the next choice smaller. Sitting comfortably can be the whole plan for now.

relax-overwhelmed-03.text: Let the whole list stay a list. You only need to meet this next moment.

relax-overwhelmed-05.text: Try naming what feels most immediate. You do not need to solve it while you name it.

relax-overwhelmed-04.text: You can put a few things down without deciding when to pick them up again.

relax-overwhelmed-06.text: A busy mind can have a quiet moment too. Nothing here asks you to clear every thought.

relax-overwhelmed-07.text: You can lower the volume around you, if that feels helpful. One less input may be enough for now.

relax-overwhelmed-08.text: There is room for a smaller version of today. Keep what matters most, and reconsider the rest later.

relax-overwhelmed-09.text: If you need company beyond this recording, you can reach out to someone you trust.

relax-overwhelmed-10.text: You are allowed to take the next step slowly. It does not have to explain the whole journey.

relax-ground-01.text: Notice one colour near you. Let your eyes stay with it for a comfortable moment.

relax-ground-03.text: Listen for a sound nearby. You do not have to decide whether you like it.

relax-ground-04.text: Look for something with a soft edge or a familiar shape. Let that be your focus for a moment.

relax-ground-02.text: Find the place where your body meets the chair or floor. Notice that contact, without changing anything.

relax-ground-06.text: Let your attention visit your hands. Notice where they are resting.

relax-ground-07.text: Look around and find something ordinary that you had not noticed today.

relax-ground-05.text: If it feels comfortable, notice the texture of your sleeve or a cushion beside you.

relax-ground-08.text: Notice the light in this space. It might be bright, dim, warm, or somewhere in between.

relax-ground-10.text: Bring your attention back to where you are sitting. There is no need to hold it there perfectly.

relax-ground-09.text: You can keep your eyes open. Choose one steady point in the room to return to.

relax-breath-01.text: If noticing your breathing feels comfortable, let one breath come and go in its own time.

relax-breath-02.text: There is no count to keep. Let your breathing find the pace that feels natural to you.

relax-breath-03.text: You do not need a deeper breath. Simply notice the one that is already happening, if that suits you.

relax-breath-04.text: Let the next breath be ordinary. You can return your attention to the room whenever you prefer.

relax-breath-06.text: Nothing to hold, nothing to force. Let a comfortable breath pass, then take your time.

relax-breath-05.text: If breath focus is not helpful today, leave it alone. Listening to a nearby sound is another option.

relax-breath-07.text: You can rest a hand somewhere comfortable and notice the gentle movement of breathing.

relax-breath-08.text: Follow one easy breath only if you want to. There is no exercise you need to complete.

relax-breath-09.text: When your attention wanders, it has not gone wrong. Come back to a sound, a shape, or a comfortable breath.

relax-breath-10.text: Let breathing happen in the background. You can simply be here without managing it.

relax-unclench-01.text: If it feels comfortable, let your shoulders settle into a position that takes a little less effort.

relax-unclench-02.text: Notice whether your hands are gripping anything. You can loosen that grip if you would like.

relax-unclench-05.text: Let the chair do a little more of the holding, if that feels right for your body.

relax-unclench-03.text: Give your jaw a comfortable resting place. No stretching or forcing is needed.

relax-unclench-04.text: You can adjust the cushion, shift your feet, or move the screen. Comfort is worth a small change.

relax-unclench-06.text: Try finding a position you do not have to work so hard to keep.

relax-unclench-07.text: You can change position during a pause. Stillness is an option, not a requirement.

relax-unclench-08.text: Notice one place that could use a little support. A pillow or a different seat might help.

relax-unclench-10.text: Let your hands rest for a moment. There is nothing they need to carry in this clip.

relax-unclench-09.text: Your body does not have to look relaxed. Choose a position that feels comfortable to you.

relax-thoughts-01.text: A thought can be here without becoming a task. You can notice it and leave the next step for later.

relax-thoughts-04.text: There is no need to finish the conversation in your head right now.

relax-thoughts-03.text: If something needs remembering, a short note can hold it while you pause.

relax-thoughts-02.text: You do not have to empty your mind to take a break. Thoughts can come along quietly.

relax-thoughts-05.text: Let your attention return to one thing you can see. You can do that as often as you need.

relax-thoughts-06.text: A busy thought does not mean you are doing rest badly. There is no test here.

relax-thoughts-07.text: You can notice that your mind has wandered without telling yourself off for it.

relax-thoughts-09.text: You can leave a question unanswered for this moment. The pause does not need an explanation.

relax-thoughts-10.text: Let a sound in the room share your attention with your thoughts. There is room for both.

relax-thoughts-08.text: If a thought keeps returning, you might simply name it: planning, remembering, or wondering.

relax-company-02.text: Luma can keep you company on the screen while you take your time.

relax-company-01.text: Here is a gentle voice for a moment. After this, there can be as much silence as you like.

relax-company-03.text: You do not have to say anything back. This little pause asks nothing of you.

relax-company-04.text: A familiar corner, a soft little mascot, and a moment without a new demand.

relax-company-05.text: You can let this be simple. Just a voice, a comfortable place, and some room to be.

relax-company-06.text: There is no conversation you need to keep going. Listen once, then choose what feels right.

relax-company-08.text: You are welcome to stay without doing anything with this moment.

relax-company-09.text: Let this little recording be a kind interruption in your day.

relax-company-07.text: If quiet company is what you wanted, you can stop choosing clips and rest here for a while.

relax-company-10.text: You can listen again, or let the room take over. Both are welcome.

relax-pause-02.text: One thing has your attention next. For this moment, you can let your attention rest.

relax-pause-01.text: Before the next task, let there be a small gap. You do not have to carry the same pace into everything.

relax-pause-04.text: A break can be short and still be worth taking. You decide when it ends.

relax-pause-05.text: You can finish a pause without proving that it helped. Taking it was enough.

relax-pause-03.text: If you have been sitting in the same position, choose a comfortable adjustment before you continue.

relax-pause-07.text: Give yourself a moment before saying yes to the next thing.

relax-pause-08.text: You can step away from the work without turning the break into another project.

relax-pause-06.text: Let the previous task have an ending, even if it is only closing a tab or setting something down.

relax-pause-10.text: There is no need to rush the transition. Let your next step begin when you are ready.

relax-pause-09.text: Choose one small comfort for this gap: a different seat, a quiet room, or a look outside.

relax-return-01.text: When you are ready, choose one gentle next step. You can take the quiet with you.

relax-return-02.text: You can stay a little longer. Leaving this pause is your choice.

relax-return-03.text: Look around once before returning to your day. Let the room come back into focus.

relax-return-04.text: Your next step can be small. A glass of water, a message, or opening one useful thing.

relax-return-05.text: There is no need to catch up with the whole day as you leave this moment.

relax-return-06.text: If you are ready to continue, decide what deserves your attention first.

relax-return-07.text: You can end the recording and keep resting. The screen does not need to stay open.

relax-return-10.text: This quiet corner will be here when you choose to visit again.

relax-return-09.text: Let the return be unhurried. You can begin with the easiest part.

relax-return-08.text: Take a moment to notice what you need next, without making it a long list.

sleep-begin-02.text: Let the evening become a little simpler. Choose one thing you can put away for tonight.

sleep-begin-01.text: You can begin winding down before everything is finished. Some things can belong to tomorrow.

sleep-begin-03.text: There is no need to produce a perfect bedtime. A small familiar routine can be enough to start.

sleep-begin-04.text: You can set aside the day without deciding how you feel about all of it.

sleep-begin-05.text: If it suits your evening, choose a quieter activity and let the pace soften.

sleep-begin-06.text: Take a moment to make your resting place comfortable. You know what feels familiar to you.

sleep-begin-07.text: Let this be an invitation to wind down, not another deadline to meet.

sleep-begin-08.text: You do not have to earn the end of the day. You can start settling whenever you are ready.

sleep-begin-09.text: Choose a gentle ending to this part of the evening. One small ritual will do.

sleep-begin-10.text: For now, you can leave tomorrow’s whole shape undecided.

sleep-phone-01.text: If you are finished with the screen, you can put it down after this recording.

sleep-phone-02.text: You can leave the messages for a time when you want to meet them. Choose what is practical for you tonight.

sleep-phone-04.text: If it helps, place the phone where it is less easy to reach while you settle.

sleep-phone-03.text: There does not have to be one more video. You can choose an ending here.

sleep-phone-05.text: You can turn down the screen brightness for comfort, then leave the rest of the app for tomorrow.

sleep-phone-07.text: You can close this page when you want to. There is nothing here you need to watch until the end.

sleep-phone-06.text: A familiar piece of audio can be enough company. You do not need to keep looking at the screen.

sleep-phone-08.text: Let the scrolling stop at an ordinary moment. It does not need a special final post.

sleep-phone-09.text: If your phone needs to stay nearby, you can still choose to turn the screen away.

sleep-phone-10.text: Choose one last useful thing to do on the phone, if needed, and let that be the stopping point.

sleep-room-01.text: Notice whether the light feels comfortable. You can change it if that is easy to do.

sleep-room-03.text: You can keep a familiar sound nearby, or choose quiet. There is no single right atmosphere.

sleep-room-02.text: Arrange the pillow or blanket in a way that suits you. Small comforts are allowed to matter.

sleep-room-04.text: Let your resting place feel like somewhere you can stop arranging things for a while.

sleep-room-06.text: Choose the light level that feels comfortable and practical for your room tonight.

sleep-room-07.text: You might put tomorrow’s first useful item somewhere easy to find, then leave the rest.

sleep-room-05.text: If something is uncomfortable, you can adjust it. You do not need to stay still for this recording.

sleep-room-09.text: There is no special position to get right. Find the one that asks less of you.

sleep-room-10.text: You can make this space a little quieter without making it perfect.

sleep-room-08.text: Let your hands settle where they feel comfortable. The bed or chair can do some of the holding.

sleep-thoughts-02.text: You do not have to solve a whole problem at bedtime. You can choose a time to revisit it.

sleep-thoughts-01.text: If tomorrow keeps asking for attention, write one short reminder and let the note hold it for now.

sleep-thoughts-03.text: A thought can pass through the evening without becoming tonight’s project.

sleep-thoughts-04.text: If writing helps, keep it brief. A few words can be enough to remember the important part.

sleep-thoughts-06.text: You can notice a planning thought and return to the room without arguing with it.

sleep-thoughts-05.text: Let tomorrow have a place on a page, rather than asking yourself to keep rehearsing it.

sleep-thoughts-07.text: There is room for unfinished thoughts at the end of a day.

sleep-thoughts-08.text: If a worry needs another person’s help, you can make a note of who you might speak with.

sleep-thoughts-09.text: You can leave a decision for a time when you feel more ready to make it.

sleep-settle-01.text: You do not have to make sleep happen for this moment to count as rest.

sleep-thoughts-10.text: Tonight does not have to contain every answer. A reminder for later may be enough.

sleep-settle-02.text: Let your body choose a comfortable position. There is nothing in this clip to keep up with.

sleep-settle-04.text: There is no finish line in this recording. Just a little space to settle.

sleep-settle-05.text: If closing your eyes feels comfortable, you can. Keeping them open is fine too.

sleep-settle-03.text: You can listen without concentrating on every word. It is fine to let the voice fade into the background.

sleep-settle-07.text: You can stop checking whether you are doing this correctly. There is no score for settling.

sleep-settle-06.text: Let the next few moments be ordinary. No special breathing, no effort to feel a certain way.

sleep-settle-08.text: Notice something comfortable, however small, and let that be enough for now.

sleep-settle-10.text: Let the recording end without choosing another thing straight away.

sleep-settle-09.text: If you need to shift position, take your time. Rest does not require perfect stillness.

sleep-awake-01.text: Being awake can feel frustrating. You do not have to turn this moment into a judgement about tomorrow.

sleep-awake-02.text: There is no need to keep checking the time while this little recording plays.

sleep-awake-04.text: Let this moment be separate from predictions about the whole next day.

sleep-awake-03.text: If it feels useful, choose something quiet and familiar while you decide what you need.

sleep-awake-06.text: If sound is irritating right now, you can stop the clip and choose silence.

sleep-awake-07.text: There is nothing you need to achieve by the end of this recording.

sleep-awake-05.text: You can make yourself comfortable without trying to force a particular result.

sleep-awake-10.text: For now, meet the moment you are in. Tomorrow does not need a verdict tonight.

sleep-awake-09.text: If sleep difficulties keep troubling you, a healthcare professional can help you explore them.

sleep-awake-08.text: You can let the room be simple: one familiar sound, one comfortable place, one moment at a time.

sleep-reflect-02.text: You can name one thing that felt difficult without making the whole day a difficult day.

sleep-reflect-03.text: Think of a moment when you met a need, however quietly. You can let that matter.

sleep-reflect-01.text: Was there one small moment today that you would like to remember? It does not have to be an achievement.

sleep-reflect-04.text: If reflection feels like more work, you can skip it tonight.

sleep-reflect-06.text: What would you like to carry into tomorrow, and what can stay with today?

sleep-reflect-05.text: You might remember a kind word, a useful pause, or something you noticed outside.

sleep-reflect-08.text: You can end with one sentence rather than a full account of the day.

sleep-reflect-09.text: Is there a small kindness you could offer yourself before the evening ends?

sleep-reflect-07.text: A day can hold both effort and unfinished things. You do not have to choose only one story about it.

sleep-goodnight-02.text: Goodnight from Daywell. Leave the next thing for whenever you are ready to meet it.

sleep-goodnight-01.text: That is all from this little voice for now. You can let the room become quiet.

sleep-reflect-10.text: Let the reflection be brief and gentle. You can close it whenever you have had enough.

sleep-goodnight-03.text: You can put the screen away and let your own evening continue.

sleep-goodnight-04.text: Nothing else is required here tonight. Take the quiet you need.

sleep-goodnight-05.text: Luma can stay a little picture on the screen, or you can close the app. Either way, the clip is finished.

sleep-goodnight-06.text: Let this be a gentle ending, with no new instruction waiting after it.

sleep-goodnight-08.text: The words can stop now. There is room for your own quiet.

sleep-goodnight-07.text: You have permission to leave this moment unfinished too. Rest in whatever way suits you.

sleep-goodnight-10.text: Take your time settling. Daywell will be here when you choose to return.

sleep-goodnight-09.text: Goodnight. There is no need to reply, choose a score, or record anything.

move-begin-01.text: Choose a little movement that suits your body today. It can be much smaller than a full workout.

move-begin-03.text: You do not need a dramatic start. Make enough space to move comfortably, then choose one thing.

move-begin-02.text: A familiar, comfortable movement is a good place to begin. You set the pace.

move-begin-04.text: Before you begin, check that your space and equipment are ready for what you have chosen.

move-begin-06.text: A short session can stand on its own. It does not need to become a longer one.

move-begin-05.text: You can choose movement because it feels useful, without making it a punishment for anything.

move-begin-07.text: Start with something you already know how to do comfortably. New movements can wait for suitable guidance.

move-begin-08.text: There is room for a gentle version of your plan today.

move-begin-09.text: Your first step can be getting ready. Choose a comfortable place and something familiar to begin with.

move-begin-10.text: If movement is not right for you today, you can choose rest. The plan is allowed to change.

move-pace-01.text: You can slow down without ending the session. Your pace belongs to you.

move-pace-03.text: There is no need to match the pace of this voice. Move in the way that suits you.

move-pace-02.text: Keep your attention on how the movement feels, rather than how it might look to someone else.

move-pace-04.text: A comfortable, familiar pace is enough. You can adjust it as you go.

move-pace-05.text: If the effort feels wrong for you, pause and reconsider the next step.

move-pace-06.text: You can make a movement smaller or choose a familiar alternative that feels comfortable.

move-pace-08.text: Let a steady pace matter more than finishing quickly.

move-pace-09.text: You can check in with yourself without comparing today with another day.

move-pace-07.text: There is no prize for rushing through the part you are doing now.

move-pace-10.text: Choose the version you can do comfortably. Making an adjustment is part of looking after yourself.

move-rest-01.text: A rest belongs in the session too. Take the time you need before deciding whether to continue.

move-rest-02.text: Set the equipment down safely, if you are using any, and give yourself a comfortable pause.

move-rest-04.text: Let this be a pause without a challenge hidden inside it.

move-rest-03.text: You do not need to fill every gap with another exercise.

move-rest-05.text: You can take longer than you planned to rest. Your next move can wait.

move-rest-08.text: A break does not erase the movement you have already chosen to do.

move-rest-06.text: Check whether continuing feels right today. Stopping is one of your options.

move-rest-07.text: If you would like a drink, take a moment for that. There is no need to hurry back.

move-rest-10.text: Use this gap to get comfortable again before choosing what comes next.

move-walk-01.text: Choose a route and distance that suit you today. A short familiar loop is a complete option.

move-rest-09.text: There is no instruction to push through pain here. Stop if something hurts or feels concerning.

move-walk-03.text: You can turn back whenever you choose. There is no distance you owe the app.

move-walk-04.text: A few comfortable minutes of moving around can be the whole plan.

move-walk-02.text: If you go outside, keep your attention on your surroundings. This recording can wait when you need to listen.

move-walk-06.text: Choose somewhere practical and comfortable for the way you move.

move-walk-05.text: You might notice one detail along your route: a colour, a sound, or the shape of a tree.

move-walk-07.text: If going outside is not possible, you can choose another familiar movement or a pause indoors.

move-walk-08.text: You do not have to make the outing faster or longer to make it worth doing.

move-walk-09.text: Let the route fit your energy and circumstances, rather than forcing yourself to fit a target.

move-walk-10.text: When you return, you can decide whether to record the outing. It counts as an experience either way.

move-strength-03.text: Take a moment to check the space around you before lifting or moving equipment.

move-strength-02.text: Choose a manageable version of the session. You do not need a personal record today.

move-strength-01.text: Use a familiar plan and equipment you know how to handle. Ask a qualified trainer when you need help with technique.

move-strength-05.text: Give each movement your attention. A slower setup can be a useful part of the session.

move-strength-04.text: You can record the exercises and loads you choose, so there is less to remember next time.

move-strength-06.text: You can stop a set when you need to. A number on the plan is not an instruction to ignore discomfort.

move-strength-08.text: Keep your equipment and water within practical reach before you begin.

move-strength-09.text: If you are unsure about an exercise, get suitable guidance before trying to follow it from a short recording.

move-strength-07.text: Let your current ability guide today’s choices. Someone else’s routine does not have to be yours.

move-adapt-02.text: You can choose a seated, standing, or other familiar option that suits your mobility.

move-adapt-01.text: A shorter session can be a thoughtful choice. You can change the plan without calling it a failure.

move-strength-10.text: Choose one clear intention for the session, such as practising a familiar movement carefully.

move-adapt-04.text: If the space is busy or uncomfortable, you can choose a different place or another time.

move-adapt-03.text: Today’s energy does not need to match yesterday’s. Make today’s plan for today.

move-adapt-05.text: You can leave out an exercise that is not right for you. The app does not need every box filled.

move-adapt-07.text: Your circumstances are part of the plan. Work with what is possible right now.

move-adapt-06.text: A useful adjustment might be less time, a familiar alternative, or a rest day.

move-adapt-08.text: If you need support or advice for an injury or health condition, a qualified professional can guide your choices.

move-adapt-10.text: Changing the plan can be a way of paying attention to yourself.

move-adapt-09.text: You do not have to compensate tomorrow for choosing less today.

move-finish-01.text: If you are finishing, bring the session to a comfortable close using your usual routine.

move-finish-02.text: Take a moment before rushing to the next thing. You can let the session have an ending.

move-finish-03.text: Put any equipment away safely when you are ready. The next task can wait a moment.

move-finish-04.text: You can acknowledge the time you chose for movement without rating how impressive it was.

move-finish-05.text: Notice what you would like to remember for next time, if anything.

move-finish-06.text: Finishing sooner than planned is still a decision you are allowed to make.

move-finish-07.text: Let the session end without adding one more challenge just because it is available.

move-finish-10.text: Your movement time can be complete now. Choose what you need next.

move-finish-08.text: If a short note would help, record what you did and how it felt in your own words.

move-finish-09.text: There is room to feel pleased, tired, neutral, or a mixture. No particular reaction is required.

move-return-01.text: You do not need to repay the days you missed. Choose a manageable place to begin again.

move-return-02.text: A return can be gentle. Start with something familiar that suits how you feel today.

move-return-03.text: There is no catch-up session waiting here. Today can have its own small plan.

move-return-05.text: Let the first session back be about finding a comfortable starting point.

move-return-06.text: You can leave comparison with your old routine for another time.

move-return-04.text: You are allowed to be a beginner again at something you have done before.

move-return-07.text: A gap can happen for many reasons. You do not owe the app an explanation.

move-return-08.text: Choose a version you would feel comfortable coming back to, rather than the biggest possible effort.

move-return-09.text: The plan can grow later if that suits you. There is no need to decide that today.

eat-begin-02.text: You can choose something simple. A meal does not have to be a project.

eat-begin-01.text: What food is available and practical for you right now? Start with that, rather than an ideal meal.

move-return-10.text: Coming back can start with opening your plan and choosing one achievable action.

eat-begin-04.text: You do not have to earn a meal through exercise or productivity.

eat-begin-05.text: If deciding feels difficult, choose a familiar option that fits your needs.

eat-begin-03.text: Give yourself a moment to decide what would be satisfying and manageable to eat.

eat-begin-06.text: There is room for convenience. Use the food and help that make eating possible today.

eat-begin-07.text: You can make a little space for your food, even if the rest of the day feels untidy.

eat-begin-08.text: Choose what works with your preferences, access, and dietary needs.

eat-begin-09.text: A meal can be ordinary and still deserve your time.

eat-begin-10.text: You can leave judgement out of this moment and focus on what is practical to eat.

eat-simple-01.text: Think of one familiar meal with fewer steps. That can be your starting point today.

eat-simple-02.text: You can use ready-prepared ingredients if they make the meal more manageable.

eat-simple-03.text: A simple assembly of foods you enjoy can be enough. It does not need a recipe title.

eat-simple-04.text: If cooking is not possible, choose an available option that meets your needs.

eat-simple-07.text: There is no need to make everything from scratch to take care of yourself.

eat-simple-05.text: You might prepare just the next meal, rather than planning the whole week.

eat-simple-06.text: Choose the easiest useful step: find a bowl, take out an ingredient, or decide on a familiar dish.

eat-simple-09.text: Let the meal fit the energy you have for making it.

eat-simple-08.text: You can repeat a meal you like. Variety does not need to become pressure at every sitting.

eat-simple-10.text: If help is available, you can ask for it. Preparing food does not have to be a solo task.

eat-pantry-02.text: A quick look at your available food can make the next decision smaller.

eat-pantry-03.text: Check what needs using, and follow the storage and date guidance on the packaging.

eat-pantry-01.text: Choose one ingredient you already have and a familiar way you like to use it.

eat-pantry-04.text: You can build your shopping list around a meal you already know you enjoy.

eat-pantry-06.text: You do not need to use everything at once. Choose what makes sense for the next meal.

eat-pantry-05.text: If an ingredient is missing, a familiar suitable alternative may keep the plan simple.

eat-pantry-09.text: Before shopping, check whether you already have the main thing you need.

eat-pantry-07.text: Let your budget and available ingredients guide the plan without turning it into a test.

eat-pantry-08.text: You can keep a short list of meals that work with your usual cupboard staples.

eat-shopping-01.text: Write down the foods for one or two useful meals first. The list can grow only if it needs to.

eat-pantry-10.text: If you are unsure whether food is safe to eat, follow trusted food-safety advice rather than guessing.

eat-shopping-02.text: Keep familiar, practical options on your list. Shopping does not need to reinvent your routine.

eat-shopping-04.text: A short list can hold the remembering for you. Add the things you know you need.

eat-shopping-05.text: Choose quantities that fit your household, storage space, and plans.

eat-shopping-03.text: You can group similar items together to make the shop easier to follow.

eat-shopping-06.text: Leave room for your budget. A useful list does not have to be an ambitious one.

eat-shopping-07.text: If the usual item is unavailable, pause and choose a suitable alternative rather than rushing.

eat-shopping-08.text: Check ingredients against any allergies or dietary requirements that apply to you.

eat-shopping-09.text: You can keep a few reliable meal ingredients on the list for busy days.

eat-shopping-10.text: When the list feels too long, start with the essentials for your next meals.

eat-notice-01.text: If it feels comfortable, notice one flavour or texture in the food you have chosen.

eat-notice-03.text: You can choose a comfortable place to eat, if your day allows it.

eat-notice-04.text: Let the meal have a little space in your day without grading it.

eat-notice-02.text: You do not need to turn eating into an exercise. A small moment of attention is optional.

eat-notice-07.text: You can enjoy a familiar food without making it a reward you had to earn.

eat-notice-05.text: If noticing food closely is not helpful for you, you can simply eat in the way that suits you.

eat-notice-06.text: There is no perfect pace to match in this recording. Take the time that feels practical.

eat-notice-09.text: You do not need to compare this meal with someone else’s plate.

eat-notice-10.text: Let the words finish, and give your attention to whatever makes eating feel manageable today.

eat-notice-08.text: A meal can include comfort, convenience, culture, and enjoyment. It does not need one single purpose.

eat-log-02.text: You can leave numbers out and keep a simple note about your meal.

eat-log-01.text: If you want a record, write what you ate in the amount of detail that feels useful.

eat-log-03.text: A food record can help you remember practical things, such as a meal you would like to make again.

eat-log-04.text: You do not need to label the meal good or bad to remember it.

eat-log-05.text: If tracking food feels unhelpful, you can skip the record and keep using the other tools.

eat-log-06.text: You might note what made the meal easier today, rather than giving it a score.

eat-log-07.text: A short description can be enough. The record is for you.

eat-log-09.text: You can use your history to find meals you enjoyed and practical ideas for later.

eat-log-08.text: If you are unsure about an amount, avoid treating a guess as an exact measurement.

focus-start-01.text: Choose one thing you can begin without solving the whole task first.

eat-log-10.text: Before saving, check that the words say what you want to remember.

focus-start-02.text: Make the first step concrete: open the document, find the tool, or write one sentence.

focus-start-05.text: If starting feels difficult, make the starting action smaller.

focus-start-04.text: Pick a piece of the task that fits the time and attention you have right now.

focus-start-03.text: You can start with a rough version. It does not have to look finished yet.

focus-start-06.text: You do not need a perfect plan to take one useful step.

focus-start-07.text: Put one task in front of you, and let the rest stay on the list for now.

focus-start-08.text: Choose what you are beginning, then decide how long you would like to try.

focus-start-10.text: The next action can be small enough to describe in a few words.

focus-return-01.text: You noticed your attention moved. You can return without telling yourself off.

focus-start-09.text: You can begin with preparation if that is the step that helps you move forward.

focus-return-03.text: A distraction does not erase the work you already did.

focus-return-02.text: Find the next small action in your task. Begin there, rather than restarting the whole plan.

focus-return-04.text: If a thought needs remembering, put it on a short later list and return when you are ready.

focus-return-05.text: You can close one unnecessary tab if that makes the next step easier.

focus-return-06.text: Take a moment to remember what you meant to do next. There is no rush.

focus-return-07.text: You do not have to recover every lost minute. Choose what is useful now.

focus-return-09.text: Returning is part of focusing. You are allowed to do it more than once.

focus-return-08.text: If the task has become unclear, write the next action in plain words.

focus-return-10.text: You can choose to continue, take a break, or change the plan. Make that choice deliberately.

focus-priority-03.text: Choose one priority and give it a clear next action.

focus-priority-02.text: A list can hold possibilities without asking you to finish them all today.

focus-priority-01.text: Which task would make the next part of your day easier? You can start by choosing just that one.

focus-priority-05.text: Not everything that is written down has the same urgency.

focus-priority-04.text: You can move a task to another day when that is the practical choice.

focus-priority-06.text: Look for what matters now, then let the rest wait somewhere you can find it.

focus-priority-08.text: You can remove a task that no longer serves a purpose.

focus-priority-09.text: A useful plan leaves room for real life, including interruptions and rest.

focus-priority-07.text: If the list feels crowded, separate what must happen today from what can be reconsidered.

focus-priority-10.text: You do not need a long list to make a meaningful choice about today.

focus-finish-01.text: If you are stopping now, leave yourself a short note about where to pick up next time.

focus-finish-02.text: You can recognise the attention you gave, even if the task is not finished.

focus-finish-05.text: You do not need to keep going just because there is more to do.

focus-finish-04.text: What is the next useful step? A few words can save you some remembering later.

focus-finish-03.text: Give the session an ending by saving your work where appropriate and choosing a pause.

focus-finish-08.text: Choose whether to continue later or leave the task for another day.

focus-finish-07.text: A session can end with progress, a discovery, or a clearer question.

focus-finish-06.text: If you finished something, take a moment to notice it before adding the next task.

focus-finish-09.text: You can put the work down without making a promise to do more tonight.

progress-small-01.text: What is one small thing you would like to acknowledge today? It does not need to impress anyone.

focus-finish-10.text: Let a small ending be enough: close the file, move the note, or turn away from the desk.

progress-small-02.text: You can notice effort that would never appear on a checklist.

progress-small-03.text: A helpful choice can be quiet: asking for support, eating a meal, or taking a pause.

progress-small-04.text: If something felt a little easier today, you can let yourself notice that.

progress-small-06.text: A small win can be something you chose not to add to an already full day.

progress-small-07.text: You can be pleased with one step without claiming that everything is sorted.

progress-small-05.text: You do not need a streak to recognise a moment of care.

progress-small-09.text: Progress can include learning what does not work for you.

progress-small-08.text: If you would like, keep a sentence about what mattered. A sentence is enough.

progress-small-10.text: Look for something real and specific, however small, that you want to remember.

progress-lookback-02.text: Look for a pattern that feels useful, rather than a number to judge yourself by.

progress-lookback-01.text: Your history can show moments, not a verdict on who you are. Read it with some room for context.

progress-lookback-03.text: An empty day in the record is simply a day without an entry. It is not proof that nothing happened.

progress-lookback-05.text: Notice something you would like to repeat, if anything stands out.

progress-lookback-06.text: Your records belong to you. You can choose how much of the past to look at today.

progress-lookback-04.text: You can remember the circumstances around a difficult week as well as the things you recorded.

progress-lookback-08.text: You might find a small practical idea in an older note that would help now.

progress-lookback-09.text: Compare your plans with what was possible, not with an imaginary perfect week.

progress-lookback-07.text: A change in routine can tell a story worth understanding, without needing blame.

progress-reset-02.text: You can begin again without making up for every missed plan.

progress-lookback-10.text: You can close the history whenever you have learned enough for today.

progress-reset-01.text: One difficult day does not need to decide the next one. Choose what would help you now.

progress-reset-03.text: There is no debt of self-care to repay. Start with one need in front of you.

progress-reset-04.text: A smaller plan may fit better tomorrow. You are allowed to adjust it.

progress-reset-05.text: You do not need to explain a gap before returning to your tools.

progress-reset-07.text: You can keep what helped and leave the rest of the plan behind.

progress-reset-06.text: If a goal has become pressure, you can reconsider the goal itself.

progress-reset-08.text: A fresh start can happen in the middle of a day, without waiting for Monday.

progress-reset-09.text: Choose something manageable enough that it feels like an invitation.

progress-reset-10.text: You can be honest about what was hard and still make room for a different next step.

progress-next-01.text: What is one small thing that would support tomorrow? Choose something practical rather than ambitious.

progress-next-02.text: Make the next step easy to recognise when the time comes.

progress-next-04.text: Leave some room in the plan for things you cannot predict.

progress-next-03.text: You can put a reminder somewhere useful without filling the whole day with alerts.

progress-next-07.text: You can prepare one small thing now and leave the rest for tomorrow.

progress-next-05.text: Choose a time that fits your life, and allow yourself to change it if needed.

progress-next-06.text: A useful plan can include a meal, a break, or a familiar piece of movement.

progress-next-09.text: Your next step does not have to be harder than the last one.

progress-next-08.text: Decide what enough might look like, so the task does not keep growing.

progress-next-10.text: Let tomorrow begin with an invitation you would feel comfortable accepting.

everyday-hello-02.text: Welcome in. You do not have to arrive with a plan.

everyday-hello-03.text: You can start with how today feels, or simply choose something you need.

everyday-hello-01.text: Hello from Daywell. Choose a little company, a useful tool, or a quiet moment for yourself.

everyday-hello-06.text: You can take a moment before choosing. The tools will wait.

everyday-hello-04.text: There is room here for an ordinary day. Pick one small place to begin.

everyday-hello-05.text: Hello. Your next step can be practical, restful, or still undecided.

everyday-hello-09.text: Let this visit fit the day you are actually having.

everyday-hello-07.text: Welcome back to your little corner of Daywell. Choose what is useful today.

everyday-hello-08.text: You do not have to use every part of the app. One helpful thing is enough.

everyday-morning-02.text: You can begin the morning with something familiar and practical.

everyday-morning-01.text: Before the day gets crowded, choose one thing you would like to make room for.

everyday-hello-10.text: Come in at your own pace. There is no routine you need to complete before you belong here.

everyday-morning-03.text: There is no need to design the whole day before taking the first step.

everyday-morning-04.text: Notice what you need this morning, rather than what a perfect morning is supposed to contain.

everyday-morning-05.text: A slower start can still be a start. Choose what is possible now.

everyday-morning-06.text: If the morning has already been busy, you can make a small pause here.

everyday-morning-07.text: Choose one useful thing for the next hour. The rest can stay undecided for a moment.

everyday-morning-08.text: You can start with food, a comfortable movement, or checking what is planned.

everyday-morning-10.text: Let the first choice be a kind and practical one.

everyday-lowenergy-01.text: If energy feels limited, choose a smaller version of the plan.

everyday-morning-09.text: Today does not need to copy yesterday. Make room for the circumstances you have.

everyday-lowenergy-02.text: You can keep the essentials and reconsider the extras.

everyday-lowenergy-04.text: Choose the next action that asks a little less of you.

everyday-lowenergy-03.text: There is no need to make a low-energy day look like a high-energy one.

everyday-lowenergy-05.text: You can use a familiar shortcut, ask for help, or take a pause.

everyday-lowenergy-06.text: An easier meal or a shorter task can be a sensible choice today.

everyday-lowenergy-07.text: Let your plan respond to your circumstances rather than arguing with them.

everyday-lowenergy-09.text: A day with less energy still deserves comfort and care.

everyday-lowenergy-08.text: You can decide what needs doing and what can wait, one thing at a time.

everyday-lowenergy-10.text: If this is a time to rest, you do not have to turn rest into an achievement.

everyday-choice-03.text: A useful choice does not have to be the best possible choice.

everyday-choice-02.text: Start by asking what you need most immediately, rather than what would be ideal.

everyday-choice-01.text: You can narrow the choice to two practical options, then pick the one that feels easier to begin.

everyday-choice-05.text: Let one decision be small enough to make now. The others can wait.

everyday-choice-04.text: You can choose a familiar option when comparing everything feels like too much.

everyday-choice-06.text: If nothing stands out, a short pause is also an available choice.

everyday-choice-09.text: You can change your mind after trying a small first step.

everyday-choice-08.text: Choose what fits the time you have, and allow the plan to stay simple.

everyday-choice-07.text: You do not have to optimise this moment. Something workable can be enough.

everyday-time-02.text: Pick a length that feels manageable. A timer is a tool you can change.

everyday-time-01.text: You can choose a short timer to give an activity a clear beginning and end.

everyday-choice-10.text: Put aside the options that are not practical today. Work with what remains.

everyday-time-05.text: A small amount of time can have a clear purpose without becoming a challenge.

everyday-time-03.text: You can pause or end a timer when you need to. The number does not make the decision for you.

everyday-time-04.text: Decide what the timer is for before you start it: focus, a break, or a familiar activity.

everyday-time-06.text: If timing adds pressure today, you can do the activity without a countdown.

everyday-time-07.text: Keep the next stretch of time simple enough to explain in one sentence.

everyday-time-08.text: You can leave a little space between activities rather than filling every minute.

everyday-time-09.text: Choose a stopping point that makes it easier to return later.

everyday-time-10.text: Time can help hold a plan, but you are allowed to adjust the plan.

everyday-water-01.text: Would a drink be useful right now? Choose what suits you and any guidance you follow.

everyday-water-03.text: You can put something you often need within easy reach.

everyday-water-04.text: Before the next task, ask whether there is a small comfort you have been putting off.

everyday-water-02.text: Take a moment to check a practical need: a drink, a meal, a comfortable seat, or a break.

everyday-water-05.text: If you need to refill your usual drink, this can be a convenient moment.

everyday-water-07.text: You can take care of an ordinary need before getting back to the list.

everyday-water-06.text: A practical check-in does not need a score. Notice what would help and choose one thing.

everyday-water-08.text: Maybe the next useful step is simply making yourself more comfortable.

everyday-water-09.text: Choose what your situation calls for, rather than following every suggestion in the app.

everyday-water-10.text: You can skip this reminder if it is not useful. Your own needs come first.

everyday-transition-02.text: You can mark the change with something small, such as putting a tool away or moving to another seat.

everyday-transition-03.text: What belongs in the next part of your day? Choose one thing to carry forward.

everyday-transition-01.text: Let one part of the day end before you ask yourself to begin the next.

everyday-transition-05.text: Give yourself a moment to arrive at the next activity.

everyday-transition-04.text: You do not have to take the pace of work into your rest time.

everyday-transition-06.text: If a task is unfinished, a short note can make it easier to leave for now.

everyday-transition-08.text: Let the transition include a little space for what you need.

everyday-transition-07.text: You can choose a different rhythm for the next hour.

everyday-transition-09.text: There is no rule that the next activity has to start immediately.

everyday-kindness-02.text: You can name a difficulty and still speak to yourself with care.

everyday-transition-10.text: You can begin the next part of the day with one clear, manageable choice.

everyday-kindness-01.text: Try describing the situation without adding an insult about yourself.

everyday-kindness-04.text: You do not need to be harsh with yourself to choose a useful next step.

everyday-kindness-05.text: What would a practical, kind response sound like in this moment?

everyday-kindness-03.text: A mistake can be something to respond to, rather than a definition of who you are.

everyday-kindness-08.text: You are allowed to need support while working on something that matters.

everyday-kindness-07.text: Let the next sentence you say to yourself leave room for your circumstances.

everyday-kindness-06.text: You can acknowledge that something is hard without deciding you should find it easy.

everyday-kindness-10.text: Kindness can be ordinary and specific. It does not need to sound like a grand affirmation.

everyday-kindness-09.text: Try replacing a verdict with a description of what happened and what might help next.

everyday-boundary-01.text: You can check the space in your day before agreeing to another task.

everyday-boundary-02.text: A useful answer can be that you need time to think about it.

everyday-boundary-03.text: You do not have to fill every available gap with something productive.

everyday-boundary-04.text: Choose what fits your responsibilities and the capacity you have today.

everyday-boundary-07.text: You can leave one part of the day without a new commitment.

everyday-boundary-05.text: You can make a request smaller or ask when it really needs to happen.

everyday-boundary-06.text: A little room in the plan can help you respond when life changes it.

everyday-boundary-08.text: Before adding more, look at what you have already chosen to carry.

everyday-boundary-10.text: Keep some space for ordinary needs, including food, rest, and the unexpected.

everyday-boundary-09.text: You are allowed to reconsider a plan when your circumstances change.

everyday-goodbye-01.text: You can leave the app and take one small idea with you.

everyday-goodbye-03.text: Choose the next useful thing, or choose a little more quiet.

everyday-goodbye-02.text: There is nothing else you need to complete here before returning to your day.

everyday-goodbye-06.text: You can come back when you want a tool or a little company.

everyday-goodbye-05.text: Let the words end and your own day continue at your pace.

everyday-goodbye-04.text: Daywell can be a brief visit. You do not need to stay on the screen.

everyday-goodbye-09.text: The next step belongs to you. Keep it manageable.

everyday-goodbye-07.text: Take what was useful from this moment and leave the rest.

everyday-goodbye-08.text: You do not need to turn this visit into a streak. A useful moment is enough.

everyday-goodbye-10.text: A little space, a little care, and then back to whatever you choose next.
